claims.explanation: K-858 is a KIF11 inhibitor, and sensitivity is likely driven by mitotic dependency and proliferative signaling. Lines with EGFR mutation or BRAF mutation, which activate MAPK and increase mitotic entry, are enriched among sensitive lines, while loss of PTEN or NF1 may further increase PI3K/MAPK signaling and sensitize. Conversely, intact RB1 and CDKN2A may allow cells to arrest and survive, and high expression of drug efflux or survival pathways could protect.

Enriched in sensitive lines (HEC265, ZR751, UACC62, FTC133); PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and increases mitotic entry.
Enriched in sensitive lines (KALS1, S117, BICR6, FTC133); NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS/MAPK.
Enriched in resistant lines (OV7, KU1919, SNU685); RB1 loss may allow arrest and survival after mitotic inhibition.
Enriched in resistant lines (SNU1214, IPC298, NCIH1437); CDKN2A loss may reduce dependence on mitotic checkpoints.
Target expression; higher KIF11 may increase dependence on Eg5 function.
Common in both groups; p53 loss may allow survival after mitotic slippage.
